What? Only an hour at the time of writing? And no past experience? Surely this can't be an accurate review. Take of it what you will, but an hour was all I needed (and the 15 dollars to buy it.) .
Why?
DawnBringer's 32 color palette was the default palette. Considering the tiny amount of work I've done with a limited palette (no "dirty" brushes) has been with this palette, I felt at home with this program almost instantly (Disclaimer: You may not feel as comfortable as soon as you start it up like I did. Trust me, it won't take too long.) .
Ok, so the palette isn't the real reason I love it. You can set up your own anyways, just thought that was awesome.
Working with it is easy for any beginner pixel artists or anyone new to the program (like me), while still powerful enough for professional artists. The pixelated interface is a nice touch, too. Dunno why that one guy was complaining, a round/smooth GUI would look strange (If you have no idea what I'm talking about, some guy gave a negative review because the GUI was pixel art itself.) .
But what is (what I think) the one thing that makes this worth more than some free digital art program?
LAYERS AND ANIMATION FRAMES ARE SEPARATE! That makes both simple and complex animations FAR easier to make. It functions a bit like other animation programs out there (I've had a little experience in Adobe Flash). What does this mean, you might (or might not) be asking? You can edit an image in different layers (like Photoshop layers), then move on to the nexxt frame of animation, while keeping the layers of the image!
I already have a small project in mind to use this program for, too! I will take
(I made these back in an animation/image editing class. I used Photoshop for them...) and redo them (unposterize, if you will) while using the same 32 color palette.
Oh yeah, and you can make sprite sheets for games. I'll be using that one day.

Point and Click adventures are a finicky bunch; regardless of whether the genre as a whole appeals to you or not, there are always a few titles that you will love simply because of the thematic material. I personally find myself on a fine edge with the genre. I tend to get frustrated easily with the Sierra logic puzzles but at the same time I will often stick it out simply to see the next moment of storytelling. This can hold true even if the characters are not ones I have previously been invested in.

Sadly I just was not impressed by Hector. I made it maybe halfway through the first chapter/episode/adventure/whatever and just had no desire to suffer through the point and click gameplay to see the story pan out. I only briefly started the second iteration/sequel/whatever and it was just more of the same. The gameplay was by no means flawed and the art was actually rather marvelous, but Hector as a character just did not appeal to me.
Obviously I have no way to concisely convey all of my tastes in entertainment so I think my best advice would be to check out the trailers for the game, and maybe watch the first 10-15 minutes of gameplay on youtube. If you like the humor and the narrative then definitely pick up the trilogy when it goes on sale next. Otherwise, there are tons of other franchises out there to enjoy. I personally love the Wallace and Grommit titles, as well as the Back to the Future series.

I started flight sims when i was 7, with games like combat flight simulator, Crimson skies etc...
I took a huge break, of almost 3-4 years, without touching a joystick. Then I heard about this game. I bought it, plugged my joystick...
1st impression: The cockpit is amazingly alive! The way the camera reacts to the plane's movements, the vibration, all of this makes the cockpit incredibly real. The clickable cockpit adds to it.
Next, the sounds. Never heard a 7.7 MG in real life, so I can't judge this. But the engine sounds are very good.
The graphics are not incredible, but they are right, Plus, with the Team Fusion Patch, it gets a lot better.
In dogfights, you "feel" the plane. You know when it's gonna stall, when you're going to spin, and I don't know why. You just feel it. The damage models are very good, too.
And, the big plus to this game: MULTIPLAYER.
The ATAG's community is very active, very kind. Their server can host 100 guys, and, usually, 20-80 pilots are there.
To finish with, i'll recommend this game. A lot. Plug your joystick, use TrackIR, and here you are!

The story of SteamWorld Heist follows Piper, a cowbot whose ‘job’ it is to visit planets making deliveries and gathering ‘moisture’ in a time where the Royalists run everything. But Scrappers, rogue cowbots who destroy others for parts, are on the rise and terrorizing every corner of the galaxy so you decide to lend a helping hand with your crew. The story actually gets a lot more detailed within two or three missions and is really well written. So far (I haven’t completed the game) I’m loving following it and I feel it is one of the strong suits of the game if you follow it and read all the dialogue (if you don’t it’s really easy to skip it and miss what is going on). The characters and crew you meet along the way are really loveable and feel a lot more than just random soldiers or cannon fodder which comes from just how well the dialouge and small bios are written.
The gameplay of SteamWorld Heist is so freaking fun. If you’ve ever played XCOM and Worms you’ll find it melds the gameplay style of those together perfectly making for an amazing turn-based strategy that requires a lot of skill and tactics rather than luck.
You start with two crew members which you can control but you’ll be able to recruit more crew members as the missions go on. Each crew member has a class and their own stats and abilities which you’ll be able to level up as you complete missions and earn experience. Though the abilities are predefined for each class and you cannot choose how to upgrade each crew member you can choose which crew goes onto which mission allowing you to level some members first if you prefer their skills. When you begin a mission you’ll be allowed to choose your difficulty and you’ll gain experience and rewards based on whichever you select, harder reaping better benefits but also having larger penalties for failure. Once you’ve chosen your level and difficulty you’ll be able to change your loadout choosing weapons and items for use in combat that you can equip your crew with then you’re ready to battle. Weapons can be class specific or used by any class, it depends and each weapon can have different perks like added crit chance or guaranteed cripple and some weapons are rarer than others with a few not being able to be bought only found. Items can be bought at any shop and range from grenades and melee weapons to healing kits, all of which can be using during missions.
The gameplay is turn based and as I said before is reminiscent of XCOM. You can move a certain amount of tiles per turn and also have the option to attack (depending on the distance you moved). Your attacks can be controlled much like you can when playing worms, you just choose your direction and fire either directly at your target or using a little ricochet to help you along. Different weapons will attack differently, have different effects and do different damage so you’ll be able to customize your loadout to your playstyle.
Enemies you kill drop hats sometimes (hats are just superficial but for some reason I find myself wanting to own every single one) and you can find ‘swag’ throughout the levels which will reveal its content at the end of the level. This can range from new weapons for your crew, items to sell or moisture. You don’t have to collect all the items on the level but I strongly advise it if you want your game to not get too hard as you go along because everything you find can be used or sold. Stuff you don’t want can be sold for moisture meaning exploring is always the better option and you feel rewarded for not just rushing.
Each mission you start will have one or multiple goals which you’ll need to complete before advancing to the next level but you don’t always have to complete them all, some are entirely optional. Some of the missions are optional also and you can ignore them if you don’t feel like it’s worth your time or if it’s too hard meaning you’re able to play the game at your own pace rather than being forced through the motions.
--- Great easy to learn gameplay.
--- Loveable crew members.
--- Fantastic story with well-written dialogue
--- Multiple genres melded well.
--- Intuitive gameplay and interfaces.
---Procedurally generated maps for replayability.
--- HATS OKAY. HATS..
---
--- The robots ...breathe…? Meaning some shots i’ve missed because the aim changes ever so slightly without warning.
--- Can’t block, defend or set up any way to protect yourself between rounds like you can in similar games.
--- Can’t compare item stats when buying them.
SteamWorld Heist is one of those fantastic games that keeps you coming back for more and more every time. The unique way it combines multiple game styles to create such a perfect game is unbelievable and it’s yet another game I can’t recommend highly enough. The gameplay works perfectly, the story is well written and the characters are engaging. This is one of the few games out there i’d say is fully deserving of it’s price tag and worth every single cent.You’ll find SteamWorld Heist satisfying cravings you didn’t even know you had.

You definately have to be more tactical with realism focussed touches like no hud, high recoil, and slow ads times. Each weapon is very detailed with unique recoil patterns and even fire-mode selectors. A variety of attatchments add customization. Great to see a system where all players are given supply points to spend at the match start to build a kit. No progression system whatsoever! Overall great game if you are looking for a tactical, less twithchy, shooter.

Frames one the otherhand lets you create a  subsequent image you can edit. Then you can Play the Frames with a press of a button to see how well your animated sprite is coming along. Together  these features makes animation a lot more easier.
It can also open files of different image formats. So if you want to trace an image you have hand drawn, you can load it, copy it and paste it on a layer.
Even without being on sale, the price of this software is affordable.
I recommend this software. It's a buy.

*Note: I got this game for free and only played half of it. The free aspect doesn’t affect my review as if I purchased it myself, my review wouldn’t change. Also, I only played half of it because a certain aspect made me not want to play any further*
At first glance I thought this looked like a nice little time wasting Indie Casual game where you must collect gold and beat challenging levels. Thus, I thought it would be fun whilst it lasted. However, after playing for a while, my viewpoint quickly changed and here’s why:
Pros:
♦ Star system is positive to a point (The star system gives good replayability to the levels, however there are still some cons with the overall star system which I have outlined in the cons section)
♦ Random items thrown down is a good concept (This is great as it adds another fun aspect to the levels and the game)
♦ Makes use of Steam features such as Achievements and Trading Cards (This is great as you could make some of the cost back on the game from the cards and most of the achievements seem easy to get just for playing the game. However, some achievements might be hard to get due to inconsistencies and RNG.)
♦ Graphics are decent for what they are (Graphics look great for the limited graphics there are, apart from the gold which is outlined in the cons)
♦ Sound/Music is enjoyable (The music and sounds fit the time periods and game soo well)
♦ Cheap in price (It’s only $2, you may get your monies worgh but that depends if you can handle all the cons)
♦ Has multiple different language versions (Can play in English and Russian. This is nice, however there are only these two languages)
♦ Story is decent due to historical facts (I can’t back say how accurate the story and facts are as I don’t fully know my history, but they seemed to have decent factual information throughout the game)
Cons:
♦ No proper Options Menu only sound settings (No graphic settings, no resolution settings, no control settings etc.)
♦ Can’t change controls (This is annoying as you are forced to use the arrow keys and can’t use WASD at all. This is terrible because people have different setups to play games and being forced to only use the arrow keys may make the game impossible to play for some people)
♦ Sound Settings are click to adjust instead of slide to adjust (Click to adjust is bad as when you want to change sound settings you must click all the way from 0-10 and if you click passed 10, you go to 0 and must start over. This is very annoying)
♦ No way to put in fullscreen (No resolution options and alt+enter doesn’t work. Really annoying having to play a game in windowed mode at the resolution it opens at)
♦ In-Game Menu not centred to window (It’s slightly to the right and off-centre for some reason)
♦ Losing just takes you to the In-Game Menu and says, "Trolley Destroyed" or something generic depending how you lost (This is okay but could have a better death animation and loss screen rather than the menu with text randomly typed)
♦ Star System makes no sense (I beat level 1 with 3 stars. Then I beat level 2 with 2 stars. Then I had level 4 with 1 star and I had full lives and over 50% gold collected, timing might have been bad but it was almost as fast as the level would allow)
♦ RNG of items on California makes getting three stars or completing a level way harder (If less clocks are thrown down, then you won't get three stars for finishing within a starable time etc.)
♦ Movement is annoying (Moving from one side to the other to collect something falling is almost impossible. Also, moving from mid to the side is a challenge. There are speed up items randomly thrown in but these are few and far between)
♦ California 1-5 almost impossible to beat and star (This is due to poor timing to beat the level and because RNG of items thrown down clocks are random per play through. Therefore, getting bonus time to give you enough time to finish the level/get the time star is almost impossible)
♦ Bombs are hard to avoid (Avoiding bombs is almost impossible as their exploding area is rather large and when you’re trying to avoid multiple rocks at the same time, it makes it even harder to avoid the rock and the bomb making you have to avoid one or the other)
♦ English punctuation on cut scenes not the best (This is due to punctuation being all over the place)
♦ Voice-Overs would’ve helped immensely (This is because having to read the text yourself takes away from the story they are trying to portray in my opinion)
♦ Every cutscene has the same picture per place (For example all of California has the same picture and all of Australia has the same picture etc. They should have switched it up for each level)
♦ On California, difficulty scales way too fast (This is because it goes from 90 - 80 - 67 seconds and then on the last level you’re struggling to have enough time to win. Similar with Australia levels one and two are really easy and then the third level ramps up the difficulty too quickly. Their needs to be more of a gradual difficulty increase in my opinion)
♦ Australia way easier than California but Africa RNG of ore is bad (Australia was easier than California as you didn’t have to worry about the time aspect same with Africa. However, Africa was harder than Australia due to RNG of the ore but still had no time issues to worry about like in California. In my opinion since it goes California, Australia and then Africa etc… shouldn’t the game get harder as you progress to new places? And not harder because the game is buggy/built poorly but because of difficulty).
♦ Too easy to be stuck in a lose lose situation on Australia 2-5 (This is because if two bombs are thrown or a bomb and rock are thrown and the kangaroo is near, you dodge the kangaroo but the bomb explodes and you collect the rock causing you to lose multiple, if not all your lives. Also, having the bamboo grow and not be destroyable when it's fully grown traps you and almost ensures your death as you can't destroy it and have to wait for the miner to shoot rocks/gold to where you are trapped)
♦ RNG of gold ore makes beating a level harder (This is annoying as some playthroughs of a level there can be more gold than rocks and other playthroughs there can be hardly any gold)
♦ Items get stuck easily on ledges especially in Africa 3-3 (This is annoying as you really need or want to collect something and they just build up on a ledge and you must wait for something else to push the item or ore off the ledge)
♦ In California levels there is a gap on right side of the level that if anything falls down that path, you can't collect it (This is annoying and shouldn’t happen)
♦ Gold is just a glowing particle (It doesn’t look like ore at all which is annoying as it’s being mined)
♦ Looks and acts like a buggy, rushed and unfished Flash Game (I could probably find similar and free flash games on the internet, that are made better)
Overall, the game is $2 and you may get your monies worth if you can get passed the difficulty issues, control issues, screen size issues, the RNG of the whole game and the star system being inconsistent etc. However, even though the game is cheap and you may get your monies worth, there are far too many easily fixable bugs and things that have been left out etc in this game that make it feel like an unfinished, rushed, flash game that I’d find for free on a flash game website. Therefore, as there are more cons than pro’s and the fact I could find similar and better free flash game on the internet, I can’t recommend this game in its current state.

One arena level, an island, surrounded by deadly water, where you running in circles, shooting and dodging waves of similar, endless, and damn fast big jumping and exploding balls. Then, one ball is spawning right after you and you're -95 health (out of 100). And then next ball is just jumping that high that you just don't see it until it hits your head. Right in top of it. Death from above.
There are three modes. First, "Survival": you just running from one crate (with one of 3 guns, or health boost, or ammo), which is stading right on the island sand, to the next one. Second, "Economical" mode, is about 100$ per kill, and insta-buys. Just click the button - and voila - the prize is yours! The catch is... that you need to actually catch that prize that you've just bought, and the blasting balls even on the 1st wave are much faster than you. Third, and the last so far game mode, is about standing at one place and shooting with the machinegun in all directions. Simultaneously. There's no "flying" mode so far, you can't shoot those balls on the fly-by, as the last video from the store page is showing.
Honestly? It's a garbage "Arena" game, made with Unity engine, and there are, sadly, maybe hundreds games like this on the Steam store these days. However, I must admit, "Boom island" is trying. Trying really hard to be not like the others. There is a peculiar soundtrack, somewhat "original" visuals, fitting the supposed setting of the early 1900's and black-and-white cinema. The "options" screens, especially "visuals", are really touching, with all those anti-aliasing and such. However, the game is unplayable at moment. It lacks the very, very basic option to tune - the mouse sensitivity. You see, not only those exploding balls are running faster than you, and spawning right after your back or above you. The main problem is that it's the game where you need to constantly spinning around. And by the standard, you're turning right as fast as the weather vane... when there's no wind around.
So - No. It's not just "rough on the edges", as someone said about it earlier. It's a garbage that some creative man is trying to present as the art object. Mark 4/10. I'd refunded it... but I was gifted with this "game". Guess it will stuck in my inventory now.

Smash together XCOM and Worms and you get Steamworld. Or to put it better: take tactical combat system from XCOM and insert it into a game of Worms. If you played either and enjoyed it, then I'd recommend this game for you.
Graphical design is great, sounds and music are fitting the atmosphere, story is sufficient to keep things going, there's a moderate variety of enemies, an occasional boss fight and replayable randomly generated missions. The missions are plentiful, replayable and hand out semi-random loot each time. Missions are almost all randomly laid out, with the objective and some elements staying the same on each replay (layout of boss rooms, or rare loot drops for instance). The game has some elementary rpg elements (you collect a crew of individuals who level up and you get random and potentially rare gear to equip them with, there are simple dialogues that flesh out characters and so on) but not enough to call it an rpg on its own. You won't make any major decisions or pick from dialogue options, or assign points on leveling up, but I didn't really miss any of it honestly because I was too busy having a good time during the missions.
To sum it up It's a tactical squad turn-based strategy and a damn good one at that. Very user friendly, difficulty options to accomodate both new players or skilled ones and a pretty unique space-western-steampunk atmosphere. Worth the full price.

Metrico+ is a piece of art wrapped around a 2D puzzle platform video game. Metrico+ starts off by choosing between a male or female character. From there, your character enters a world built around obstacles that you need to overcome. You start off with basic controls giving you the ability to move left and right along with a normal jump function.  The only way to continue on to the next part of the world is to get to the end of the level. The environment is what makes Metrico+ a unique puzzle game. The actions you do with the character alter the environment around you. This is what allows you to continue on your path or prevent you from going any further.
In one puzzle, a simple jump can make one pillar go up and another come down while moving left in the air can force a platform to move right.  This created some fun moments of myself jumping up and down in hopes the environment would change into my favor. However, controlling your character excessively can quickly create more problems and easily stop you in your tracks.  Digital Dreams was kind enough to create a beautiful labeling system that highlights vital information improving your ability to make decisions.  Each puzzle is well thought out and I found myself smiling every time I reached the end of a level. The puzzles become more complex and challenging requiring you learn from your mistakes and to think creatively.

Metrico+ is a game for those who just couldn’t get enough out of their statistics class! Welcome to Metrico+! Where platforming and puzzles meets Info graphics and pie charts. In Metrico+, you’ll explore a multitude of worlds, solve puzzles, listen to some pretty sweet music, and think outside the box! But the question remains, is Metrico+ worth your time?
The basics of the gameplay are fairly simple. You play as random generic guy and or girl. As ‘random generic guy and or girl’, it’s your job to platform and puzzle-solve your way to victory throughout each of the six worlds. With every world, you gain a new ability to change the way the world and it’s puzzles react and as such, you gain more difficult and more challenging puzzles to solve. Each world is based on the set of skills you gain and with that in mind, each world’s puzzles become more challenging with more steps involved as the level progresses, as well as adding in skills you previously learned. In the beginning of each world, the puzzles are simple and are introductions to the main character’s new skills. As the puzzles progress, the puzzles involving those skills become more challenging.
There’s a nice sense of progression in each world, and furthermore, the entire game. Individual puzzles don’t have the cohesion that I feel they need in order to master any one particular style of puzzle, but they all play out in interesting ways that make up for their lack of core cohesion with each puzzle by making each world’s difficulty ramp better. With that being said, the ‘featured’ ability you gain in each world often takes precedence over previously learned skills, and a few skills the player ends up learning aren’t used nearly as often as others.
There’s also the ability to quit and return to any individual checkpoint or puzzle in the map area. It’s a nice touch that means people who aren’t into puzzles (or for those who don’t play 1 game until it’s finished) can go back at any time to any puzzle of each world, rather than just the worlds. It’s a nice touch to include for more casual puzzle-game lovers into the universe of Metrico+.
The only thing that will kill the game is it’s replay factors. While it’s a wonderful 2-4 hour experience, there’s little reward to replay the game, making it a bit pricey compared to other platformers in a similar price point.
Visually, the game is very beautiful to look at, and the idea of basing a puzzle platformer on graphs and info graphics is a neat concept. The vibrant colors combined with the simple visuals make a nice and appealing game. The background takes full advantage of it’s 3D and adds infographics and pie charts galore. That being said, it’s visual style is purely that, and it doesn’t take any true advantage of the math portion that it might have if it focused the style more on game integration, rather than it simply being a reactive world. With that, it is interesting how the background reacts to the player and his or her decisions. In fact, we didn’t actually notice it until the second or so world in. A nice, stylized touch.
As for audio and sound, I love it. The musical soundtrack is simple, in a ‘what you probably think your math teacher likes’ sorta way. The world’s reactive style also lends itself to the audio effects. Everything the player does makes a sound, and it’s hard to describe because it plays well into the musical background pieces. It’s interesting hearing the sounds you make while solving the puzzles blend into the music so well.
Control wise, the game is fairly straightforward. I played with  my Lunar Xbox One Controller, but it also worked fine with a 360 Controller, and we also played a world with keyboard and mouse. The controls seemed to work fine with their transition from PlayStation Vita to PC. Settings wise, there are some basic graphical and resolution settings, as well as options for things like Depth of Field and Vsync. The frame rate also appears to be locked at 60fps. The UI also appears to have been unchanged from the Vita version of the game it rather suffers for it if I’m frank. It doesn’t look terrible, but it could have used a new menu layout to accompany it’s PC release.
For Metrico+, it’s a fun game that suffers from replayability and the passage of time. Once you play through the game once or twice to master the puzzles, there’s little to really keep players coming back. It’s a short, fun 2-4 hour experience, but it suffers from the fact that it leans on it’s puzzle elements too much compared to the platforming elements, making replayability rather difficult for a game like this. For me, the game is great at what it does, but it’s lack of replayability makes it rather difficult to suggest at $13.99. If you’re not fully sold on the game by now, wait on a sale. As is, Metrico+ is a great game with a great visual style and great soundtrack that suffers from lack of replayability. If the developer decides to add something like Workshop support and custom levels, then consider the game a solid full-price recommendation from us.

A bit overwhelming to the first time player, though luckily there's both an in-depth text guide and interactive tutorial to help you get acclimated.  Both the RTS and Flight Simulator aspects of the game impressed me.  While I haven't spent a lot of time trying out the RTS side of things yet, I do appreciate the ability to slow things down, issue orders, and speed things back up again.  There are also a lot of different commands available that you can assign to individual ships.  The flight sim side reminded me a bit of Battlestar Galactica in the sense that you can strafe in one direction while pointing in another (by turning off smart thrust).  The ability to switch off between different ships is a nice touch too.  There's a lot here for the $15 price tag and is thus an easy recommend.

My first foray into the hybrid FPS/RTS was Battlezone, and I've not encountered anything that compares to the unique experience it provided - until I played Void Destroyer. The combat feels tight, the RTS gameplay rewarding, and everything in between just -feels- right. Bravo on a fantastic game, a truly worthy successor to my Battlezone experience!

A very strange visual novel, but a deeply engaging one nontheless. A combination of highly intricate world-building and Suda51's unique brand of style has produced what is quite possibly his strangest, and most certainly his most underrated, game of his career.

The Silver Case is a fantastically intriguing crime drama. Suda's world building is impeccable; he explores both the personal stories and the struggles of complex multi-organization bureaucracy when finding the truth. There's a right balance of "getting the player up-to-date" and "showing, not telling" to this story. It's a world you want to know more about.
The game is defintiely archaic, including its controls, but it is definetly managable. To be honest, I found it a little charming for a product of its time. While some may find the linear 3D sections pointless for how rail-roady they are, I'm perfectly okay with the more physical investment they supply for the player's relation to the story. My only true complaint to the 3D sections is that they aren't really filled with that much world building; most of the actual world building comes from mandatory dialaogue.
Overall, this is a game I think is essential to play if you are a fan of Suda51, seeing the birth of his style of game.

An old game, that I actually only recently discovered, but I am glad I did!
To get the obvious things out of the way : yes, the graphics are quite dated, even compared to games of the same era (such as Half Life 2, which of course was cutting edge at the time), the menus and saving system are not quite user friendly, and the AI is a bit dodgy.
But other than that, they managed to hit a home run on most of the other aspects of this game, and the overall atmosphere of the game is exceptional.
Right from the opening scenes and sequences the game gets you, and makes you see through the rough 3D models and effects. The dramatic music, appropriate lighting (that also dares to go nicely dark where needed), detailed sound design, and engaging and interesting storyline comes together effectively to bring an immersive and believable feeling to the game, even when playing it now.
Furthermore, the gameplay and game mechanics are very well done and feel like a contemporary game. The possibilities for controlling and commanding your team are, at first sight, not enormously extensive, but they are effective and provide an enjoyable and challenging gameplay. Although it might turn out good sometimes, most fights should not be rushed into without some tactical planning! And beware of the incredible difficulty spikes every now and then, throughout the campaign you will encounter some unexpectedly complex and difficult battle situations.
In short: if you can see through the few shortcomings, it rewards you with a highly enjoyable, sometimes challenging, and immersive gaming experience

I'll grant my review is biased because I am a SW fan and have played 90% of the videogames in the franchise. And yet, for a 12 years old game, it's quite good. At the time this was released I was playing Halo 2 on my xbox primarily, and I remember getting the demo of Republic Commando and being impressed by it (sadly I never bought it before now).
The story is not short, unlike many more recent FPS, and even at a fast pace it takes some 10 hours to complete it. The levels are extremely linear, but I guess nobody expected otherwise back in 2005.
Some aspects in the game amazed me, and really convinced me the team behind RC worked hard and with passion to make it a very polished game. For example the characters have deep-enough personalities and countless situational dialogue lines, the animations are many, diverse and realistic, the enemy AI and especially the squad AI are excellent. At some points in the game I almost thought the other Delta Squad members couldn't be computer-controlled, because their movements and behaviour were customised depending on the situation.
Given it's very old, and that now most of the cash flows into Disney's pockets, I advise getting it during sales. Generally I consider a game with a ratio of gametime in hours/price in euros bigger than 1 to be worth the cost, and I bought this at 75% off. But even at € 9.99 it feels like a good purchase according to my "rule".
One last note is that multiplayer is doable, but requires using other softwares. There are no servers up at all times, so you must get in touch with people who play regularly and see if you can join their matches.

Purchased Aseprite through HumbleBundle because I didn't know it existed on Steam. It works for Steam, HumbleBundle, and requires no real installation. What I mean is that after the first installation, there is really no need to use Steam to run Aseprite. Windows recognizes its file extensions and you're pretty much set. For more complex spriting, I still prefer Photoshop but Aseprite makes it a lot easier to animate considering you don't need to identify Layers and Frames as two separate Windows as you would in Photoshop.
Aseprite is a dedicated spriting platform much like how Painter is a dedicated Painting program. Photoshop is robust but like Painter, Aseprite makes it easy to sprite things on the fly without having to go through a lot of configurations.
+ Recognizes most shortcuts Photoshop uses
+ Easy to remap shortcuts
+ Color code selection made easy
+ Frames and Layers in one window
+ Frames and Layers are easy navigated by Arrow Keys
+ Multiple windows within one window
+ Exporting made easy; includes interlace option, animation loop option, scaling option up to 1000% without anti-aliasing
+ Tagging your frames so you can have idle/run/shoot/etc animations on one timeline; making it possible to play specific animations on that timeline, these can be color coded as well
+ Cycle through animations with < and >, I had this setup in Photoshop but since it came like this in Aseprite by default, I was pretty happy about it
+ Runs a lot more efficiently than Photoshop, obviously dedicated pixelart/spriting platform
+ Live symmetry, option where you can draw both sides at the same time vertically or horizontally
+ Live tiled preview, option where you can make seamless textures easily
+ Animated tiled preview and symmetry view
+ Custom brushes made easily (feels glitchy sometimes)
+ Dithering made really easy
+ Anti-aliasing tool that gives you blurred effect like brush
+ Sprites automatically backed up, made to recover lost sprites
+ Ability to paint within the same shading so you don't go outside the pixels
+ Onion Skin; this option gives you the ability to see a less opaque version of the previous and next frame allowing for easy transitions and animations
+ Not intense on the system's resources
+ Pixel perfect option performs where you won't get a distortion in the pixels forming the right amount of pixels between lines. However, this can be an issue if you're trying to fill in a color or paint a chunk of pixels somewhere.
- Arrow keys don't move pixels or objects unless selected by "Marquee" or "Select All" so you need 3 more actions for it
- Aseprite files don't transfer to anything else well
- Can not have windows outside of Aseprite's window (can window full screen it to all your monitors though)
- Wish there was an easy option to export frames via tags

I can honestly say that I have not played a platformer like Metrico+. Developed by studio Digital Dreams, the game is equal parts unique design and aesthetics. Its unusual style may put some people off, but this could be literally the most fun you'll have with bars and graphs.
Doing Business:
You are a silhouette running through a world of graphs, pie charts and more. Your only objective is to reach the end of each area, when even more weirdness will occur.
The game is a mix of puzzle solving and platforming built around figuring out the way to move forward. Objects will react differently to certain actions: Are you moving, are you jumping, are there enemies left, and more. The puzzles are confined to single screens; allowing you to process everything in front of you.
You'll start with just moving your character around, but things grow as you get further in. Each level in the game introduces a new mechanic or twist on a previous one.  The mechanic twists help to keep the puzzle-solving constantly evolving.
For instance, in one level you'll make use of moving platforms based on your motion on the ground or air. Even the act of dying and restarting a puzzle will become a part of puzzle solving.
The player must figure out the rules of each situation and use them to their advantage. How things respond in one area will change; forcing you to adapt.
For players who want more challenge, each level has optional mysterious challenges that you'll need to figure out what you need to do to complete them.
The aesthetics of Metrico+ are amazing and grow from looking like a business PowerPoint presentation to a surrealistic landscape and more. The only problem that I have with Metrico+ is that it may be too minimalistic at times.
Limited Landscape:
Metrico+ is a game that leaves everything to the player to solve. This can be both good and bad in terms of motivation. Without guidance, it's up to the player to push through to solve the myriad of puzzles. Due to the rules constantly shifting (even within levels), it can be a little frustrating to start at zero with each section.
An important point about Metrico+ is that it's a puzzle-platformer. Because the game requires equal parts skill and puzzle solving, this can make some puzzles extra difficult. You may get stuck because you haven't solved the puzzle, or that you know the solution, but aren't doing it right. Metrico+ never approaches the skill level of games like Mario or Super Meat Boy, but it does require you to be reasonable at platforming.
The theme of Metrico+ is definitely mysterious, and if you aren't willing or able to dive into it, the game will be over for you quite quickly.
I would love to talk more about the puzzles directly, but any attempt at talking about them would take us into spoiler territory.
Growth over Time:
Metrico+ is very much a platformer all its own. The puzzle designs constantly change to keep you guessing and help to make things varied. If you enjoy puzzle-based games, definitely give this one a look, but I can't tell you if it will make you fall in love with bar graphs.

NOTE: This game was given to me by the developer for review purposes. This did not influence my review in any way.
Metrico+ is a two-dimensional scrolling puzzle platformer with a mathematical theme, evolved from a hand-held console game from a couple of years ago.
You play a man or woman (your choice) in a weird, dream-like world made up of platforms, chart components, and geometrical shapes, many of which move in response to your own actions.
Graphics - Metrico+'s graphics are quietly impressive, from a minimalist perspective. The game's backgrounds don't immediately jump out as being anything special, but as I played I found myself drawn to watching them to see what changes were wrought by my actions. Each world has a different feel to it, but they're all very nicely crafted.
The character graphics, too, are excellent. Your chosen man or woman is shown in silhouette, in what looks like a fairly low-polygon model, but which looks very nice. Animation is fantastic -- motion capture, I assume -- and your character moves very fluidly about the platforms.
The platforms themselves are sufficient, if nothing spectacular. They do their job well enough.
The interface is minimal, with a few very occasional and discreet panels introducing new controls as they become available, and menus with simple symbols rather than any text. In fact, I don't think the game features any text at all, apart from percentages and fractions in game that make up part of the platform puzzles. I found it reminiscent of Monument Valley on Android in this manner, although they're very different types of games.
Sound - The first thing I noticed about the sound in Metrico+ was the music, which was excellent. It begins with a sort of minimal oriental theme, and works its way through a number of ambient themes as the game progresses. It's very pleasing to the ear, doesn't distract from the game, and I didn't find it becoming boring either.
Sound effects are appropriate and work well with the game. I've not encountered any voices, but there are some sampled sounds for certain character actions and events, such as jumping.
Gameplay - Metrico+ is a group of connected series of geometric puzzles with themes based on metrics, most of which boil down to lowering, raising, or otherwise moving platforms based on following certain movement patterns.
For example, on one screen, moving to the right might move one platform to the left and fill a column moving to the right, jumping might raise one platform, and landing might raise another by a different amount. To solve each puzzle you first have to work out how each component responds to your various actions, and then work out how to make your way across the screen to the other side, using those actions to move the platforms where you need them.
The game starts out easy, with only left and right movement, jumping, and falling available to you. After completing the first world you gain another available action, and the platform level puzzles become more complex. This continues with each world that you complete.
Although there seems to be no story to speak of, the weird map that progresses as you finish each world, and the progressive changes in your character, hint that there may be more to the world of Metrico+ than is obvious. After the third world you're given a choice of two different ways to proceed, too, and I'm not sure what effects this branching has on your progress through the world.
At this point I've only played up to the fifth world, I think, and I've hit a level that I don't yet know how to complete. I hope it will come to me, as I don't want to stop my exploration of Metrico+'s strange world yet.
Metrico+ features Steam Achievements, too, but they're all hidden. In a couple of hours of play I've only managed to gain two of them; this is one game that I won't be completing to 100%.
Pros:
+ Excellent graphics with a consistent 'feel' to them
+ Character graphics and animation are particularly great
+ Pleasant music in a few different themes
+ Steam Achievements
+ Full controller support (I played exclusively with an Xbox 360 controller)
+ Very high production values
Cons:
- It seems a bit expensive to me
- Hidden Achievements are a bit annoying
I found Metrico+ to be a rewarding experience. If you enjoy puzzle platformers and being forced to think in a different way, then Metrico+ may well be for you, although the price may put you off a bit.

Metrico+ is a rather unique singleplayer puzzle platformer game designed around graphs and statistics. As silly it may sound, it works. Number of jumps controls one platform, going forward controls another, number of enemies killed controls that and that. Each puzzle takes anything from 20 seconds to 3 minutes to solve but none are just "too hard" for you to figure out. Once you try everything you can do, you figure out what controls what and then you simply build the simple solution in your head and execute it. The game consists of 6 worlds each with around 16 puzzles I believe. The game introduces you to new mechanics of the game every new world so it never gets too boring or tedious.
The asthetics of the game are gorgeous. Almost fluid-like background with great selection of colors that does pleasing result.
The story of the game... I believe there is none, although there is abstract concept in between the worlds you can interpret on your own. However the lack of story is not important and doesn't bother at all.
Metrico+ can be finished within single one or two sittings. I have 7 hours played, but the game took me around 3 to 4 hours to finish. There's some extra content in doing optional challenges in some puzzles and of course, achievements.
I've played this with Xbox 360 gamepad and the Steam Controller, both well suited for this type of game.
Game has little to no graphical settings apart from resolution and general quality settings, but then again, not an issue for 2.5D platformer.
Current price of 13.99€ might seem a little bit much for a rather short game with limited replay value and that's up to you to decide.

The Silver Case is one of Suda51's earliest works, repurposed in HD for Steam and consoles. It's an investigative game with small puzzle elements and bits of "walking sim", if you will, where you'll literally have to just look around and go from point to point. It's setting is a modern Japan, in one of its many prefectures, with a main character that finds himself suddenly moved between old fashoned police work and special units to assist in the capture and\or execution of Kamui, a super serial killer causing a big commotion among the populace.
Of course, as per Suda's tradition, the plot dwells deep into pseudo-mystical themes, totally absurd propositions, or ridiculous devices. It usually works, but you must keep in mind this is a 18 years old game with some cosmetic adjustments here and there. It is most definitely no Killer7, and its themes and main plot are really uninspired if compared to its author's usual standards.
I will say it immediately: this game has two main problems. The first and most glaring issue, is that its Boring. Boring as hell. I kept going to see when it would finally pick up the pace, but it never really did. The ending was a letdown, this type of plot has been done to death and I really wanted it to be reverted or get a surprise ending of some sort, but it's just your token end that you will no doubt see from a mile away. Characters are not even developed past one or two sentecens, that is, if they are not important. The only character that has some meaning in the story (and you can count on it, he will survive through the end of course) in the most developed, and barely the only reason to keep playing some sections.
The second issue is in the gameplay aspect. Yes, it's a PS1 adventure game, but there is absolutely no excuse, even for the standards of the time. This should have been a classic Visual novel rather than a walking sim on rails, it takes an eternity to do anything and the the brief intermissions with the puzzles seemed more of an after thought, put in there just to make the game artifically longer. The last chapter in particular was a chore to sit through: there's a tower with 10 levels to ""explore"" to trigger an event, and each and every room has meaningless pieces of paper inside or absolutely nothing. But you have to visit every room to progress.
At least I liked the music, the remixes as well, although it had just a couple of tracks in total, could have used some more. A small selections of scenes were decent, the second and fourth cases were somewhat interesting.
For all the love I have for Suda51's works, I cannot recommend this game at all. The plot is decent, not good, just decent, the pacing is unnecessarily slow and the gameplay is pointless busywork. If I had to put a score to it, it would be a 5\10.

There are things you should know before buying The Silver Case. First of all, the controls and the puzzles are real bad. During the vast majority of the second half of the game you literally just keep waking up, taking a step forward and then use your computer to read emails. I am not joking. Like, why even have this riveting 'gameplay' in the first place? Thankfully, at least the puzzles can be skipped. Also, the plot is unnecessarily confusing and the whole game feels like a bad fever dream at times.
And yet, despite of these shortcomings, I enjoyed the game immensely. This game brings me to my childhood, back when the whole world was mysterious and full of things waiting to be discovered. Turns out there is still lots of crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥out there. The confusing plot is still more interesting than 90% of the other video games plots. I liked most of the characters, but wished I could have interacted with them in more meaningful ways. The game also features a lot of glorious 90s 3D graphics and FMV. The game has a lots of style and atmosphere, which is enhanced by the excellent soundtrack by Masafumi Takada.
The Silver Case is an unique experience and if you can stomach visual novels with bad gameplay, you are in for a good time. I got this during the sale, but it would have easily been worth the full price.

Raunchy and amazing toilet humour in the most British of ways is the order of the day with these titles, and it's everything an (im)mature young adult could possibly want. This point and click puzzle game, consisting of three episodes is absolutely hilarious. It has this typical, dark, British humour (think of Blackadder). The puzzles are neat and if you reaaaaally have no idea how to solve it, it has a hints system. It will continue to mock you too if you use said hint system. Get it.

Note that even if the title says "Hector: Episode 3", the review is for the full 3-episode series.
Detective Inspector Hector is sort of like The Dude. He's the right man for his place and time. Hector is a cop in the degenerate town of Clappers Wreake, a place which has so abandoned the notion of anything wholesome that the street out front of the police station itself features ♥♥♥♥♥s, drunks, and looting.
And so the story is set in motion: a sniper appears in a window in town, gunning down police and boasting a roomful of hostages. Hector is called to the scene to deliver his unique brand of justice, only to be set on a series of errands for the mysterious gunman who claims only to have the betterment of Clappers Wreake at heart.
Hector is fat, blunt, rude, an alcoholic, and not a connoisseur of self-respect. He's every ounce as much of a degenerate as the rest of the population, but he's smarter than a good deal of them, and he's willing to do what it takes to save the day. For... well, some reason or other, anyways.
Hector: Badge of Carnage contains a lot of crude humor. The first screen of the first game involves fishing in a disgusting toilet with a used condom. But there's an interesting wit about it - particularly in Hector's observations on the situation. Yeah, this series is for the immature, through and through. But it's a sarcastic immaturity that's aware of its actions, and doesn't just settle for, "Look, poop, ha ha!" as an entire joke.
The voicework is not a highlight. The first game sounds as though it's voiced entirely by one guy speaking into his laptop's built-in microphone. The second game adds a genuine female voice to the cast, but that's still only two voices, seemingly digitally altered to sound more diverse. At the very least, the delivery's good, so it's nothing that'll ruin your experience.
On the whole, the puzzles are decent enough. The third game has a habit of making new elements appear in locations you've already visited, and then not alerting you to them, so that you have to stumble across them in a fit of random, confused wandering. But overall, I like Hector: Badge of Carnage. And if, like me, you're both an adventure game fan and a scumbag, then you probably will, too.

This game is fun, and has just the right length. I played the campaign for about 9 hours (including quite a bit of trial and error in some nastier segments) and I feel that would it be any longer it would start to get boring.
The cooperative aspect in the game comes in the shape of three other clone troopers in your squad, and their AI is decent. Most of the time they take care of themselves making sure to stay behind cover, and usually they pick sensible positions in the battlefield. They aren't fully self-suficient, and I think that's alligned with the narrative, being the player the one to direct their actions as a commander. They quickly respond to your prompts, and do a good job at it - if you issue them to take aggressive postions, they will move forward to face the danger regardless if you are there (but not diving madly into enemy lines). If you issue them to group up with you, they stick to your butt and babysit you quite effectively. You can perform most of the specialist actions that your squad members can do as well, which lends some nice flexibility to the gameplay. However, the spots where you can set up those actions aren't that many per battle arena, and their usage is very straightforward, making the game devoid of any deep or complex layer of strategy. The time when you set up some actions and how you support whoever is performing them is still key to your success, so it isn't brainless or anything like that - it's just that I was left wanting some more. But I guess it's a pretty decent system for a 2005 game.
There are no Jedi powers, no Force users, just gunplay and tactical action, and for that I commend this game. That shows the confidence the developers had in exploring the Star Wars universe without having to resort to these elements, and the game isn't lacking anything for it.
On the subject of gunplay, the game is constantly reminding you how the Delta squad you lead is a covert operations team, but it bothered me that it never felt too much like that was the case. Most of the time, even if in the narrative you are trying to infiltrate somewhere on a low-profile, the gameplay always devolves into frontdoor break-ins, with guns blazing. There aren't any stealth elements (I don't even think crouching helps to not attract enemy aggro) and the whole "covert" theme never really comes to life.
The map design is very linear, with very few occasions when you can take flanking postions with sneaky alternate paths. However, the combat areas are usually quite large, and there is some room for tactical maneuvering and repositioning. Overall, the combat isn't difficult, with a few spikes here and there, all of them reasonable and still nothing to pull your hair over. You will, however, die a lot if you don't learn to prioritize your targets, as some enemy types are far more dangerous than others - and your companions won't assess that level of danger on their own. As I said, the AI isn't self-suficient, and you need to command them. If you sleep on the job, a flying Geonosian will fry your entire party while they focus some droid grunts. The game expects you to be on your toes when it comes to reacting to threats and it is great for it, otherwise the gameplay would get boring very, very quickly.
Another layer of challenge comes in the form of resource management. This is much more prominent in the late game. You have to save your hard hitting ammo and grenades for the tankiest and more dangerous enemies, or you're gonna have a bad time. It's still very reasonable (it's nowhere near as unforgiving and restrictive as Resident Evil 4) and you still have some room for error.
The weapon variety is pretty tame, but it's quite sufficient for the duration of the campaign. I haven't tried the multiplayer, but I imagine it would get stale very quickly in a PvP scenario.
Overall, it's a fun little game, not too long, and if it's on sale you should most definitively check it out. For it's full price, I don't know, I feel like there are other options out there that give more bang for the buck. If you are a Star Wars fan, then definitely play this game, as it's one of the classics for this franchise.

Note 1: this review is about the singleplayer only.
Note 2: I have more hours in this game than Steam shows.
Battlefield: Bad Company 2, what can I say. It's just another Battlefield. A pretty enjoyable one for someone who doesn't usually play the 3 leading shooters on the market (CS, CoD and BF) I must add.
PROS:
+ Satisfying gunplay with decent variety. The guns look and sound good, so spot on
+ Being able to pick any (unlocked) gun you want pretty early in the game. I just like taking whatever suits my playstyle and the game won't force you to use the loadout you start with
+ Lots of different environments. Missions go through the snow, mountains, desert, jungle, urban, fields, etc.
+ Variety of missions and combat. You're mainly on foot (which is a good thing in my eyes) but you'll also be driving around in vehicles such as humvees and tanks. Usually you're following a route on your map but there's also missions in which you sort of freeroam and decide where to go first
+ Runs very decent even on lower-end machines. I happen to own a not-so-great PC yet I can get a steady ±60 fps on medium-high settings
CONS:
- Bad difficulty distribution. Take for example the first mission Cold War, making your way through the village is a walk in the park even on hard, but the driving sequence requires perfect shots if you want to make it through. Or the save points in Sangre Del Toro that are spaced out too far; they make you play it obnoxiously save because you're done playing it over and over again
- Which leads to my second con: bad save locations in already annoying missions. Using the same mission for example again, the village pretty much saved you around every corner but the driving sequence has
. This really adds up to the frustration factor
- Audio issues. I've played this game on about 3 different PC's and on every single one have I experienced the audio messing up on certain areas. Sometimes the voice acting not in sync with the subtitles, sometimes it's the guns lacking sounds, sometimes the environments don't make any noise, etc.
- Wonky self-hitdetection. Especially in driving missions you sometimes don't get hit at all and then you take like 10 hits in short succession and die. Another is to die completely out of the blue when barely hurt, even on easy. On top of that, the enemy really likes to target nobody but you, on top of your teammates barely hitting anything yet remain unharmed on the frontline. It's unpleasant
- Cutscenes are not skip-able until you've beaten the associated level. Minor con honestly, but some cutscenes are over a minute and having a bunch of them is kind of annoying
What else can I say. Neat little shooter with a few minor issues. Overall I look back at it positively.

I have to give this game a thumbs down. Not because of a bad story, or poor graphics, or even because it doesnt capture the Shadowrun feel. It has no trouble in any of the above areas. The reasons it gets a thumbs down: 1) Solo playability after the story. I know "mmo title" but I do not play games to socialize, I play MMO type games because of availability of larger selections of content that I can play alone. I do not mind helping someone who is stuck on something or is in need of help, but by and large I prefer the solo experience. Solo ends with the story so there is zero replayability for me. 2) Connectivity issues are a going concern with this title at the moment. I had a day where I was dropped from the server AT LEAST 6 times mid mission. Now, the game doesnt kill your character when the mission drops it just ends the mission. The problem here is repeating the same few minutes of a mission until the server stabalizes enough for you to actually enjoy the game. The most recent patch did very little to address this issue as it claimed to have done. 3) Like EVERY game released now days it is an incomplete title. I truly miss the days where you would receive a game (yes even an mmo) that was a completed game. Now it seems we are relegated to basic game frameworks with "pay as you play" patches, downloads, and endless unwanted updates. JUST PRODUCE A FINISHED GAME. If it needs a patch to resolve a bug or two after that, fine patch it but dont disseminate drips and drabs of a whole game when that is NOT what I've payed for. Anyway great gameplay, good story, good graphics; zero replayability.

Everyone compared this game to HBS' Shadowrun Returns game when it was released for it's similar turn-based stratagy combat. I'm sure the devs knew it would and I'm going to be pointing some of these similarities out the least I can for this review. I picked this up during the steam summer sale so getting it at a discount might be swaying my opinion yet when I think about the content I've played through so far(30 hours) the original $30 price doesn't seem too much. And there IS alot of content, or should I say missions. I don't normaly play MMO's but when I do they seem like all they are is just a bunch of fluff and filler to spend your time. Go here and collect X 20 times over. Boston Lockdown has very little filler and the exellent story keeps you going. This game really draws you in and makes you FEEL like a runner alot more than HBS' Shadowrun. This Shadowrun lets you taylor your character from look to cloths to archtype. Your character is yours, not some premade runner made by the devs or someone from the workshop community. When you enter the HUB you can interract with other runners(players) and go on combat missions with them. Combat is what you would expect with a turn-based stratagy game like HBS' Shadowrun or (more so) XCOM enemy within. I prefer this game over HBS' Shadowrun for acouple reasons. You can turn the camera to get a better view of the battle, which leads to more strategic positioning than HBS' Shadowrun. The ability to mold your character more freely also leads to more options on how you approach battles. The battles also seem to provide more of a challenge than HBS' Shadowrun but thats more of a skill thing from player to player. Other reviews have complained about the voice acting. I can understand why they would complain but for one this is not a AAA game so how can expect that much, second I'm one who enjoys some cheese now and then, watching Kevin Sorbos' Hurcules after a night of drinking is just good times man good times. It really is disappionting some people would let that get in the way of this exceptional story. This game is the closest thing to Shadowrun tabletop in a video game and I applaud Cliffhanger Games for thier effort. User generated maps is the best way to keep this game going and I so hope it keeps going, it's extremly addictive. If you like Shadowrun or just turn-based stratagy in general try this game!

I was only introduced to the Shadowrun Pen and Paper system recently. Go figure, someone born in the 80's who is only just now being introduced to SR. Anyway, here goes.
I don't know if it's just the fact I don't care enough about Voice Acting to be hypercritical about it in this game like some of the reviews I have read, or if I just haven't found any fault in it as of yet. Still playing the game, so I'll have to keep listening. Although, for me, the only thing Voice Acting is good for is to make it so I don't have to read the text myself.
As far as the Skill system is concerned, I like the utter freedom you get when playing the Pen and Paper system, and yes the SR: Returns Skill system gives you a bit more freedom than the system present in this title, but I like the choices you have to make. It forces you to build a cohesive character rather than one that can be all things to all people. Why am I going to be this physical powerhouse that can at the same time finesse his way through the entire game. In a single player game, it's fine to max out everything. In a multiplayer game, you have other players to fill in the holes left by our character concept.
As for the gameplay, it plays almost identically to SR: Returns. You have your allotted movement and actions. The only difference being you could perform an aggressive action and still move after in SR: Returns. In this you have to do your moving before any aggresive actions. So far, I am pretty enamored of the mechanics. I haven't come across the hazards others talked about as of yet.
So far, I am throroughly enjoying this game.

I'm a huge fan of the Shadowrun universe and I have thoroughly enjoyed playing all of the other Shadowrun titles on steam.
This game, however,  is disappointing in two distinct ways:
-As a game in general-
It lacks all kinds of polish. The ones that annoyed me the most is no shortcut keys and  a weird in-combat zoom in that would sometimes hide enemy movement. Oh, my mistake, there is actually one shortcut key: Enter allows you to move the dialog along when you have no conversation options (which is about 95% of the time), but ONLY once you have clicked it first. I can't explain how annoying it is to press Enter and expect something to happen and then pressing it a few more times and then realizing "Oh, yes. It only works once I've clicked it."
-As a Shadowrun title-
Don't get me wrong, there are some good character and story bits in the game but it is a far cry from any of the other Shadowrun titles. There doesn't seem to by any character development.  For most of the time that I played (which I'll admit is not very long) I have not seen any conversation choices and the few I have encounter you can't really call 'choices' because there is only one.  Everything has been boiled down to the most basic it can get. Anything that isn't shooting has now been reduced to clicking an icon that you find from time to time on you missions and cyberdecks now function just like a gun. You literally can shoot someone for real damage outside of the matrix with your cyberdeck, which is good I guess because outside of cut scenes  the matrix doesn't seem to be part of the game.  And as far as I can tell, all summoned creatures (drones, spirits ect.) share cap within the party. You can only have 2 things summoned at any time.
I must add that I'm not entirely sure about the matrix thing as I have not played a lot.
-=Conclusion=-
If you are looking  for a turn based RPG, it's quite lacking and I would recommend looking elsewhere. I suggest any other Shadowrun title on steam, Blaggards or Wasteland 2.
If you are looking for a Shadowrun game, it's utterly atrocious. I recommend you send angry letters to the developers OR pretend this failure of a Shadowrun title doesn't exist and move on with your life.
PS.
There is one other thing about the game I feel I should mention. It's a shared world, meaning it's like an MMO. You get to see all the other players running around your game and you can go on mission with them and so on. Now this is not really for or against the game but nobody wants to see a shotgun wielding, lingerie wearing, transvestite troll named 'Pen!s'.
Edit: Really, Steam? I can't even say P E N I S. What if it's his given name?

This is a reluctant reccomendation.  Pick it up on sale, and only if you have played Dragonfall and the other titles, and feel like you just want more, and/or have a few friends that you really want to go shadowrunning with.
It is important to note that the 'Director's Cut' is actually the original game plus the first DLC in one convenient package.
The story is linear, the mechanics are oversimplified, and the customization has a few wonky quirks.  Still, you *know* you want to see how Boston is holding up in 2072.  The answer is, holy Landsdowne street kid,  Fenway is still standing!
If you are a New Englander, the accents are done well enough, but the pacing will make you feel like you are suffering kids reading paragraphs aloud in 4th grade all over again.  Real southies running shadows would be talking about the Sox at least twice as fast, and with more cussing. There are enough fun culture references to crack a smile though.
Overall, the game plays the way you would expect from user generated content - not a published, full price release title.  I do enjoy user generated missions and campaigns, so it's not a coffin nail.  The developers are still updating the game, so it may pay to keep an eye on it too.
The big big redeeming cookie is multiplayer turn based strategy, so hopefully your significant other is cool rolling a decker to debuff your targets, or vice versa.
You will want to play this if you have already played the other Shadowrun titles and want another good story, or you have some runner friends you trust enough to watch your back, or you have some *ahem* fond memories of adventures in the combat zone....

Edit: 1/10/2015
Since I started playing the game again after awhile, I thought I'd update my review on this game.  (It truely deserves an updated review)  First of all, the dev has CLEARLY put in a TON of effort into the game.  Although, I find it hard to fault a game that has such a devoted creator, this game gets the best of both worlds with addictive gameplay and constant updates.  The game not only runs smoother than in the past, but actually has a battle editor now, with tons of new units and more to come.  Even the clunkiness I mentioned in my original review got attention.  The only thing I feel is missing now is multiplayer, as I would LOVE to play this game with friends.
So heres a bit about the game:
You are essentially a commander that can give orders like any space RTS style game, only you can take manual control of anything from the largest capital ships, to the capital ships indivdual turrets, to the smallest fighters (Either built or launched from a carrier).  The whole feel of the game is very unique, and it has newtonian style physics.  The models are all pretty detailed, and the gameplay is what brought me back to check out how this game has been updated.  I love games like Sins of a Solar Empire, Homeworld, and Elite Dangerous, and if you like any of those games, you will love this one too.  Just be sure to go through the tutorial when you buy this game, as there is A LOT to learn.
Conclusion:
Its addictive, its refreshing, and I'm glad I payed $15 for this game.  Buy it without hesitation if you see it on sale.  If you like space games, you won't regret it.
The devotion the dev has show towards improving his game, as well as the actual improvements made to the game makes me want to update my score out of 10.  You don't get many indy devs who will show that they care about their game (if you keep up with gaming current events, you know what I'm talking about).  That is why, for $15, I am updating my score to a 10/10 (up from an 8/10).  You will probably get more hours out of this game than some AAA titles for a quarter of the cost.
Original Review:
This game IS NOT 100% finished, but it is still a fun game to play.  Keep in mind that pretty much all of this game has been done by 1 person (if I heard correctly), so my review is rather forgiving.  The story is fairly challenging, the UI, however, is rather complicated.  There are some things in the game in terms of camera movement and overall functionality that make playing it somewhat of a hastle.
EG:  double clicking a unit both centers the camera on it and selects all similar units, which makes you move your camera back to where you want to give them the order to go.  Another example of this is trying to give an attack order on a unit that is very far away.  You basically can't right click said unit because the detection area is so small (or non existant in some cases), so you have to manually move your camera over so your view is closer.
Clunkiness aside, if (or when) this game gets multiplayer, I will definitly be buying another copy to play with a friend.  I like the graphics and the overall feel of the game.
If you want a completely done and polished Homeworld 2 only with the ability to directly take control of every craft, this isn't the game for you.  Though it definitly feels inspired by Homeworld, it lacks quite a few finishing touches.  Like I said, despite the thousands of hours put into making the game, there is like literally 1 person doing all the work.
Reading all of the patch notes the developer seems really devoted to making this game a success, so I will definitely be following this game as it progresses.
All in all, I am having fun playing the game, and if you like space battles as much as I do, you probably will too.  It just needs a few finishing touches, but a lot of the game is there.
8/10,  Always glad to put a little extra money in the pocket of an indy dev.

Visual novel detective story, with conspiracies and strange psychic elements as you might expect from Suda51.
Dialogue, music, graphics and gameplay are all very 90's style in a way.
The mood and a lot of the game comes down to a nice synth soundtrack by Masafumi Takada.
Gameplay and visuals are intentionally clunky to adhere to the original PS1 game. However the remastered 2D character art and user interface are pretty stylish and hold up well. The original Silver Case tried to break from usual visual novel mold a little but player interaction is still extremely minimal. There are a few simple puzzles but you basically push buttons to proceed the story. Much of the story is text only with little character art.
The story is more grounded and easy to understand than something like Killer 7. It has structure as a detective story without taking into account supernatural or unexplainable events. It certainly gets confusing at parts and unexpected twists might throw your preconceptions out of the window but that's what keeps it exciting. The game may have a tedious start but when the story picks up and characters gain some depth it's not messing around.
Playing through all scenarios in The Silver Case will take you around 14 hours, though don't expect to swallow the story as quickly. I thought it took more than 2 hours for the story to really pick up so the refund period might not show much. A couple puzzles at the start seem purposefully annoying to throw you off but that doesn't remain the case.
I believe whether or not you'll enjoy this game comes down to if you enjoy the central storytelling and background music. The other things are on the side though fitting as a whole. Expect the gameplay aspect and 3D graphics to be clunky but charming in their own way.
PS. I recommend doing the Placebo chapters as soon as you unlock them because of how the game is structured

Cliffs of Dover is an excellent World War 2 flight simulator, recreating what it is like to be a British or German combat pilot during the Summer of 1940. HOWEVER, it is excellent only if you use the Team Fusion patch. Let me make that clear. Cliffs of Dover should have been an excellent product from the first. Its vision and the designed scope of improvement over other WW2 flight sims was, and still is, truly next generation. However, the sim was a commercial flop - for a variety of reasons.
More than anything, the effect its release had on the flight simming community was to generate at first epic anger, and later, epic sighs of disapointment. We all had high hopes, but they were decisively dashed after the initial boot-up of what has become known as IL-2 CloD. Frame rates when the sim was first released were slide-show poor, stability was enough to make Job tear his hair, and menu navigation was inexplicably difficult. These and a myriad of other major issues kept anyone from feeling they got their money's worth. Most who had purchased Cliffs of Dover, eagerly expecting the best WW2 sim experience possible, quickly shelved it after vigorously (and justly) lambasting the developers online. The issues with which this product first shipped are unacceptable for any entertainment product if it is going to succeed. And, therefore due to the quality, or lack of it, succeed IL-2 Cliffs of Dover did not. The vision was there, the scope was there, the basics were there - but the execution left all the positives absolutely irrelevant.
Now fast forward in time to the present. Over the years since release, a series of patches from the developers have addressed many issues in the software, partly to silence their critics, but also in an effort to salvage their reputation for further software development. The most recent developer's patch, however, came with a statement: No More Work Will Be Done. Although the official patches fixed many issues, serious flaws still remained unaddressed. Seeing that CloD had been abandoned by the developers, a small group of historically-minded flight sim enthusiasts took it upon themselves to fix the glitches that remain, adding content as well as restored functionality. The result has been, literally, a game-changer. Frame rates are at 60FPS on modern machines, flight modeling is impressive, software stability is great, and the single player campaigns have even been re-written. Multiplayer is fantastic. 50 to 100 human pilots routinely fly together, in one server, over the English channel and French and English countrysides, re-enacting the dramatic days before, during, and after the Battle of Britain. You can find your aerial combat fix nearly any day or night on the ATAG (TF) multiplayer server. Team Fusion continues to poll the community for needed changes, and to add more content and bugfixes regularly. Their forum, and their patches, can be found at:
I highly recommend IL-2 CloD if you are a serious WW2 flight sim enthusiast. To date, it has the highest degree of period engine and flight modelling that a complete WW2 flight simulation product  has delivered. You will feel as if you are piloting a piston-powered, 1200 horsepower, state of the art (for 1940) aircraft into realistic and deadly combat using nothing but a compass, high-power guns, crosshairs gunsight, and your wits. It is not an easy sim. It is a realistic one. If that is what you want, you have found it. Just make sure you use the TF additions. -Venturi
